title: Study of Sleep Hygiene Index and Sleep Disturbances in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) Patients Referred to Rheumatology Clinic in A Hospital in 2024
abstract: The chronic and disabling nature of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), as well as its own pathogenesis, is associated with the likelihood of developing psychiatric and neurological disorders, such as mood disorders, anxiety, and sleep disturbances. This study aimed to investigate the sleep hygiene index and sleep disturbances in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The statistical population consisted of 50 SLE patients referred to the rheumatology clinic of Ardabil hospital. Data were collected using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Sleep Hygiene Index (SHI) questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and analytical statistical methods in SPSS version 24. 50 patients with lupus were studied for sleep problems. The mean age of participants was 43.9 ± 12.64 years. Ten patients (20%) had a history of taking sleep medications. 90% were female and 85.4% lived in Ardabil city. Mean BMI: 27.35 ± 5.27. Mean disease duration: 10.58 ± 6.59 years. Mean sleep hygiene score: 7.92 ± 3.91. Mean total sleep score: 5.92 ± 3.52. Male patients had significantly higher sleep disturbance scores than females (11.8 ± 3.7 vs. 7.5 ± 3.72). Sleep hygiene scores were significantly higher in those with a history of sleep medication use (10.5 ± 4.17 vs. 7.28 ± 3.61; P = 0.018). Sleep hygiene scores were significantly lower in patients with hypertension (2.5 ± 1.73 vs. 8.39 ± 3.68; P = 0.003). The sleep quality of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus in Ardabil province is unfavorable. Intervention strategies and health recommendations are needed

title: Analysis of the Safety Factor and Mechanical Properties of a Weight-Reduced Gearbox using a Simulation Study
abstract: The design of engineering components always includes two parts: component design and material selection. Additionally, gearboxes are key components in the power transmission system; therefore, great care must be taken in their design. In the present study, an attempt has been made to present a new design for advanced gearboxes. Two ferrous and non-ferrous alloys were selected for gear and component materials, and mechanical analyses were performed on them. SolidWorks software was used for the design. The results showed that the selected steel and titanium alloys are close competitors in terms of mechanical properties and safety factors, and both materials can be used in specific design conditions. However, due to the lighter weight of titanium compared to steel, designers are advised to conduct further studies in the field of developing components for various industries with non-ferrous alloys, as they play an effective role in reducing fuel consumption, conserving energy, and continuous improvement in various industries and products

title: The Effect of Water Vapor Content on the Reynolds Number of an Air-Water Vapor Mixture Flowing through a Horizontal Air Duct
abstract: The following article presents a study on the effect of the water vapor content in air, considered as a two-phase mixture, on the Reynolds number during the flow of an air–water vapor mixture through a horizontal air duct. More specifically, the article provides an analytical description of the mathematical model that relates the change in the Reynolds number of the air–water vapor mixture flow to the relative humidity of the water vapor. The study focused on the possibility of controlling the Reynolds number of airflow solely by adjusting the relative humidity of the water vapor in the air. The mathematical model was applied for air velocities ranging from 0 to 128 m/s, relative humidity levels from 0% to 100%, and air temperatures from -40 °C to 150 °C. The figures and study’s results indicate that increasing the relative humidity level of the water vapor leads to a decrease in the Reynolds number of the air– water vapor mixture as it flows through an air duct. Additionally, it is possible to control the Reynolds number of the flowing air–water vapor mixture solely through the relative humidity of the water vapor in the mixture. This capability is particularly useful in a wide range of industrial processes

title: The Clinical and Epidemiological Characteristics of Patients with Vitiligo: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Vitiligo is the most common depigmenting disorder worldwide, with an estimated prevalence of 0.5% to 2%. Few studies have assessed its epidemiology in Iran, and none specifically in Ardabil Province. This descriptive cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the epidemiological profile of vitiligo patients in Ardabil during the second half of 2022. All patients suspected of vitiligo and referred to a dermatology health center were clinically examined by a dermatologist. Those with a confirmed diagnosis completed a checklist covering variables such as age, sex, occupation, marital status, education, residence, family history, patient complaints, lesion site and pattern, and systemic diseases. Two hundred vitiligo patients participated, including 104 women (52%) and 96 men (48%). The highest frequency was among those over 40 years (28%). Most patients (94%) lived in urban areas, with 43.5% from Ardabil Province. A positive family history was reported in 29% of cases. The most common involvement sites were upper extremities (76.5%), lower extremities (60%), and head/face (58%). Lesion patterns were generalized (75.5%), focal (20%), and segmental (4.5%). Fourteen percent had systemic diseases, primarily hypertension (6%), thyroid disorders (4%), and diabetes (2.5%). The study identified nearly equal gender distribution and an increasing disease frequency with age. Most patients were unemployed or housewives, married, and had education up to diploma level. Urban residence predominated. Family history and generalized lesion patterns were common. Hypertension and thyroid disorders were the most frequent comorbidities among Ardabil vitiligo patients

title: Chemical Components and Biological Activities in Lilii Bulbus Based on Scientometrics: A Review
abstract: The inheritance and utilization of "homology of medicine and food" have become the focus of the society and the market. In order to avoid the singularity of traditional reviews, the scientometric method (software "CiteSpace") was used to conduct visual knowledge graph analysis and summarize the existing Chinese and English literature on Lilii Bulbus at home and abroad, and predict the research hotspots of Lilii Bulbus. There are 235 chemical components in Lilii Bulbus, including 111 steroidal saponins, 17 polysaccharides, 14 flavonoids, 21 steroidal alkaloids, 53 phenylpropenoid glycerides, and 19 other chemical components. The biological activities of Lilii Bulbus from extraction methods, compounds, models, and effective concentrations were summarized. In addition, scientometric software analysis shows that the research on Lilii Bulbus can be classified into five categories: chemical components, biological activities, species origin, quality evaluation, and methods of extraction and purification. It is worth noting that the identification and assessment of chemical components (like steroidal glycosides) of Lilii Bulbus and their biological activities (such as anti- inflammatory and antioxidant effects) are the current research foci for Lilii Bulbus research. To sum up, Lilii Bulbus, which is homologous in medicine and food, has great potential in the treatment of cancer and inflammation and can also be used as a cosmetic raw material of natural origin to deeply explore the efficacy of cosmetics and increase the added value of products

title: Surgical Management of Posterolateral Tibial Plateau Fractures: A Comparative Study of Direct Lateral and Posterolateral Approaches
abstract: Posterolateral tibial plateau fractures are challenging injuries of the knee joint, which is essential for weight-bearing and stability. These fractures typically occur due to high- energy trauma and involve complex surgical management due to the proximity of neurovascular structures and surrounding ligaments. This study aims to compare the clinicaloutcomes of two surgicalapproaches—direct lateral and posterolateral—for the fixation of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures. A descriptive was conducted on 54 patients who were evenly divided into two groups. One group underwent the direct lateral approach, while the other received the posterolateral approach. The primary outcomes measured included the International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) score, Lysholm score, range of motion, neurovascular injury, fixation success, and quality of joint reduction. Patients treated with the direct lateral approach showed significantly higher IKDC scores (92 ± 2.4) compared to the posterolateral group (90 ± 1.3), with p < 0.001. Similarly, the Lysholm scores were better in the lateral group (96 ± 2.4) versus the posterolateral group (88 ± 1.5), p < 0.001. The range of knee motion was also superior in the direct lateral group (130° vs. 125°, p < 0.001). Neurovascular injuries were fewer in the direct lateral approach. The modified direct lateral approach offers better clinical outcomes compared to the posterolateral approach, minimizing neurovascular risks and improving joint reduction and fixation. This method provides a safer and more effective surgical option for managing posterolateral tibial plateau fractures

title: Revolutionizing Type 2 Diabetes Care: Scientific Journey of Fiber Rich Cookies Made from Green Unripe Jackfruit and Sorghum Flour
abstract: Artocarpus heterophyllus (jackfruit) used in the formulation is the best way to control or maintain blood glucose levels. In small intestine, the high levels of fiber in jackfruit slow digestion by interacting with sugar, cholesterol, fat, and decrease their absorption in the body. The formulated supplement mainly contains gluten free sorghum flour and date syrup which is rich source of vitamin B complex along with seeds that have antioxidant properties. These ingredients also help to improve the nutritional efficacy of the product, prevent heart diseases, and maintain blood glucose levels. Together, these components minimize the quick absorption of sugar and offer a balance of macronutrients, making your cookies a healthier choice for diabetics. Evaluated parameters include general appearance, qualitative tests, patient acceptability, HbA1c tests (blood glucose level tests), and more. Additionally, these cookies exhibit a lower glycemic impact compared to traditional ones, making them a more desirable option. The inclusion of green unripe jackfruit in the formulation of cookies results in low glycemic index, whichcould potentially, provide health benefits for individuals suffering from degenerative diseases such as diabetes mellitus. The incorporation of functional ingredients like green unripe jackfruit, dates, and sorghum in the development of novel products holds great promise for the food industry. From this study it can be concluded that, this approach not only helps reduce waste, but also presents opportunities for cost reduction in the production of baked goods. The use of unripe jackfruit in cookie manufacturing addresses both environmental concerns and economic efficiency in the baking industry

title: Comparison of the Accuracy of Three Instruments (APACHEII, SOFA, and MPMII) in Predicting the Mortality of Patients in Intensive Care Units
abstract: Accurate prediction of mortality in intensive care units (ICUs) is vital for patient management and resource allocation. Among the most widely used scoring systems are APACHE II, SOFA, and MPM II, each providing valuable but variable estimates of patient outcomes. The present study aimed to compare the accuracy of these three instruments in predicting mortality in ICU patients. This cross-sectional study (2020) included 150 ICU patients from Ardabil University hospitals. Eligible participants were adults (>18 years) with ICU stays ≥24 hours, excluding burn and cardiac surgery cases. Data were gathered using demographic forms and APACHE II, SOFA, and MPM II questionnaires. Statistical analyses (SPSS v23) applied descriptive statistics, t-test, correlation, sensitivity, and specificity. Among the studied patients, 85 were male, with a mean age of 60.74 ± 19.62 years. The average duration of hospitalization was 10.17 ± 10.34 days, and 52 patients died. Logistic regression showed that hospital type, gender, age, length of hospitalization, duration of intubation, diagnosis, and GCS were not significant predictors of mortality. Predicted mortality was 32.21% with APACHE II, 32.50% with SOFA, and 64.01% with MPM II. Sensitivity and specificity values were 83% and 48% for APACHE II, 79% and 46% for SOFA, and 73% and 50% for MPM II, respectively. In conclusion, APACHE II demonstrated higher accuracy compared with SOFA and MPM II, and its application is recommended as the preferred prognostic tool in ICU settings

title: Advances in Polymer Synthesis and Properties: Current Trends and Applications
abstract: Polymer is the term for a large group of compounds made up of many smaller molecules. Almost every industry uses polymers. Plastics, cotton, rubber, wool, and Teflon are all types of polymers. The fact that cellulose's infrared absorption spectra are very similar to those of a spectrum that comes from space is proof that cellulose really does exist. The cellulose pellicle is the outer layer of the material. Most elastic materials, like the metals used in springs, show elastic behaviour because their bonds are stretched out. When rubber is relaxed, it has many places where long polymer chains connect to each other in a coiled shape. The main goal of polymeric delivery systems is to deliver drugs in a way that is either controlled or continuous. Polysaccharides have also been used to make drugs more concentrated in the colon after they are taken orally. Polymeric materials could lead to many interesting new uses in the not-too-distant future. A lot of different businesses are finding new uses for polymers

title: Beyond Adhesives: The Multidimensional Role of Colophony in Industry and Medicine
abstract: Colophony, commonly known as rosin, is a natural resin derived primarily from coniferous trees like pines. It is composed predominantly of resin acids, particularly abietic acid, along with a neutral fraction. This complex mixture serves as a versatile industrial raw material, with applications in adhesives, cosmetics, paints, inks, soldering fluxes, and medical products. Its eco-friendly properties, renewability, and affordability have earned it the designation green oil. Despite its extensive usage, colophony poses potential health risks, including allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) and occupational asthma, primarily due to its oxidized resin acids. Diagnosis and prevention of these adverse effects remain challenging. Modified forms of colophony, while reducing some allergenic components, may introduce new sensitizers like maleopimaric acid. Colophony also demonstrates significant pharmacological activities. Its derivatives exhibit wound healing, cytotoxicity, antimicrobial, anti-mosquito, and spasmolytic properties. Research highlights the antimicrobial potential of resin acid derivatives against bacteria such as S. aureus and E. faecalis, as well as its anti-mosquito efficacy through insect growth-regulating compounds. The chemical diversity of colophony is influenced by its source and extraction method, with α-pinene being the primary monoterpene in natural varieties. However, synthetic and regional differences contribute to varied chemical profiles. Future research should address the prevalence of ACD, optimize allergen detection, and explore additional therapeutic applications. This review underscores colophony’s industrial, pharmacological, and ecological significance while acknowledging its health risks and the need for further studies to mitigate its allergenic potential. *Corresponding Author: Anubhav Dubey; Email anubhavdwivedi803@gmail.com Eurasian Journal of Science and Technology 2026, Volume 6, Issue 2 121

title: Developing Biosorbents from Agricultural Waste: Fava Bean Shells for Efficient Dye Removal
abstract: In this study, two biosorbents were developed from fava bean shells (FBS): dried fava bean shells (DFBS) and fava bean shell charcoal (FBSC) and their adsorption performance for Congo red (CR) dye was compared. Adsorption was evaluated under varying conditions of temperature, initial dye concentration (C0), adsorbent dose, contact time, and pH. At pH < 4, FBSC exhibited superior adsorption capacity (Qe) and removal efficiency (99%) compared to DFBS (90%), highlighting the enhancement achieved through carbonization. Adsorption data were fitted to seven isotherm models; although the Langmuir model, showed high correlation, the calculated monolayer capacities differed from experimental maxima due to heterogeneous surface properties and broad concentration ranges, while Freundlich and Halsey models provided a physically meaningful description (R² > 0.9). Kinetic studies indicated that the pseudo-second-order model best described the adsorption process (R² = 0.9928 for DFBS, 0.9998 for FBSC), suggesting that chemisorption is dominant, with reasonable fits also obtained using the Elovich and intra-particle diffusion models (R² > 0.9). Thermodynamic analysis, based on dimensionless equilibrium constants, revealed that adsorption onto FBSC is spontaneous and endothermic with increased randomness at the adsorbent–adsorbate interface, whereas adsorption onto DFBS is spontaneous but slightly exothermic, reflecting moderate interactions. These findings indicate that FBSC is an efficient, economical, and environmentally friendly biosorbent for dye removal from aqueous solutions

title: The Exploratory Use of HDPE Waste Plastic for Thermal Insulation Applications
abstract: The study explored the possibility of replacing polyester polyol with HDPEPO in the development of rigid polyurethane foam as a thermal insulator. The HDPE waste plastics were prepared and pyrolysed at different temperatures (450, 475 and 500 ᵒC) to yield high-density polyethylene pyrolysis oil (HDPEPO). The effect of different pyrolysis temperatures on important physicochemical parameters, such as density, yield, viscosity, iodine value and flash point, revealed that while density increases and flash point decreases with increasing pyrolysis temperature. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analyses of the pyrolysis oil confirmed the presence of hydroxyl compounds in the HDPEPO, and their concentration decreased as the pyrolysis temperature increased, as higher temperatures promote the dehydration of alcohols to alkenes and water. The HDPEPO was used to formulate a polyurethane (PU) thermal insulator. The FTIR analysis carried out on the PU thermal insulator formulated revealed the presence of urethane linkage; however, it failed to rise, hence the need to modify HDPEPO with PEO to form HDPEPO/PEO blend. The effect of an increase in HDPEPO concentration on the crucial parameters (hydroxyl value, acid value, viscosity, and density) of HDPEPO/PEO blend revealed that the properties at 10% HDPE fall within the acceptable range. The characterisation of the HDPE-PU thermal insulator formulated using this blend is within the acceptable range when compared with the standard. The thermal insulator showed improvement in water absorptivity and thermal conductivity when compared with conventional thermal insulators. The percentage of HDPEPO utilised can be increased when PEO with a high hydroxyl value is deployed in the formation of HDPEPO/PEO blend

title: Drug-Likeness Screening, Toxicity Prediction, and Molecular Docking Study of Phytoconstituents from Salvia hispanica against HPr Kinase and Its In Vitro Antimicrobial Evaluation
abstract: This study investigates the antibacterial potential of Salvia hispanica phytoconstituents through inhibition of HPr kinase/phosphatase (PDB ID: 1KNX). Molecular docking was performed using CB-Dock2, and toxicity prediction was assessed via ProTox 2.0. An in vitro antibacterial assay evaluated the efficacy of Salvia hispanica seed mucilage against Escherichia coli by measuring the zone of inhibition at concentrations ranging from 10 to 100 µg/mL. Kaempferol and myricetin exhibited the highest binding affinities (−8.9 kcal/mol), while tocopherol showed the lowest (−7.1 kcal/mol), interacting with key active-site residues including GLU144, GLY147, VAL148 and PHE190. ADME analysis revealed log P values between −1.43 and 8.81 with most compounds classified as mildly toxic. Amikacin demonstrated an estimated LD₅₀ of 4,000 mg/kg (toxicity class 5) with potential nephrotoxic, neurotoxic, and pulmonary effects. The antibacterial activity of Salvia hispanica seed mucilage was dose-dependent; amikacin showed slightly greater inhibition at lower concentrations (10–40 µg/mL), whereas at higher concentrations (100 µg/mL), both treatments exhibited comparable antibacterial effects, producing a maximum zone of inhibition of 1.9 mm. The findings highlight several promising Salvia hispanica bioactive compounds with strong binding affinities, favorable pharmacokinetic properties and confirm the potential of seed mucilage as a natural antibacterial agent

title: Optimisation of HDPE-PU Thermal Insulation: Effect of Processing Parameters on Insulation Properties
abstract: Thermal insulation material is crucial for energy maximisation and conservation. The HDPE waste plastics were pyrolysed at 475 ᵒC. The physicochemical parameters analysis such as density, acid value, viscosity, iodine value, pour point, flash point and cloud point were carried out on the HDPE pyrolytic oil (HDPEPO). The physicochemical results agree with literature. The 10% HDPEPO was copolymerised with 90% polyester polyol (PEO) to produce HDPEPO/PEO blend. The blend was used in HDPE-PU thermal insulator production. The effect of processing parameters such as surfactant, catalyst and blowing agent was assessed on important parameters of HDPE-PU thermal insulator. The new formulation conditions established from the optimisation of processing parameters were used to formulate new HDPE-PU thermal insulator and compare with conventional PU thermal insulator and acceptable values for thermal insulatord. The properties of novel HDPE-PU thermal insulator align with and acceptable values, and show better thermal insulation and high compressive strength when compared with conventional PU thermal insulators

title: The Optical and Photoluminescence Features of GdNiSe Material Synthesized Hydrothermally
abstract: In this study, the hydrothermal method was used to synthesize the gadolinium nickel selenide (GdNiSe) material. The materials' energy bandgaps ranged from 1.58 eV to 1.18 eV. Annealing the material led to a reduction in the energy band gap. The energy bandgap of GdNiSe was enhanced through the annealing process . The photoluminescence was carried out by exposing the materials to sunlight at different time intervals. The unannealed GdNiSe material was exposed to sunlight at 20-minute intervals, ranging from 0 to 140 minutes. The prominent peaks were identified within the wavelength range of 612 to 661 nm. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis of the GdNiSe material has shown that it crystallizes in a hexagonal crystal structure with space group P63/mmc. The lattice parameters of GdNiSe are a = 0.5875 nm and c = 1.0256 nm. The XRD patterns of GdNiSe material are affected by annealing. It impacts the intensity, position, and size of peaks, revealing details about the material's structure and microstructure. The FTIR spectra showed various peaks, such as 2,654, 1,869, 1,638, 1,105, and 935 cm-1. The GdNiSe material exhibits a strong covalent bond, leading to a short bond length and high bond strength. The overlapping of their 3d and 4p orbitals creates the bond between Ni and Se, resulting in a bond order of two

title: Optical and Nanostructural Characterization of ZnO Thin Films Prepared by Spray Pyrolysis: Combined Experimental and DFT-GGA Investigation
abstract: Using a combination of experimental and density functional theory (DFT) methods, zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films were effectively formed on glass substrates by spray pyrolysis at 250 °C. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy with He–Cd laser excitation, UV–Vis spectroscopy, X ray analysis and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) study were used to investigate the optical, morphological and crystalline structure characteristics. ZnO's wide-band-gap semiconducting nature and suitability for optoelectronic applications are confirmed by the films' remarkable optical transparency in the visible spectrum and clearly defined optical band gap. The ZnO lattice's intrinsic defect states are responsible for the prominent blue-green emission bands found in PL analysis. The homogenous nanostructured surface morphology revealed by AFM studies emphasizes the significant impact of the deposition procedure on the formation of nanoscale films. The energy stability of ZnO in the wurtzite (Wz) crystal structure is confirmed by complementary DFT calculations carried out under the generalized gradient approximation (GGA), which also offer theoretical justification for the optical behavior seen in experiments. The efficacy of spray pyrolysis for creating superior ZnO thin films with promising optical and nanostructural properties is demonstrated by the great match between experimental results and theoretical expectations

title: A Comparison of the Therapeutic Effect of Euphorbia Macrolada Latex with Cryotherapy in the Treatment of Plantar Warts
abstract: Skin warts are benign tumors caused by infection of keratinocytes with HPV and are visible as hyperkeratotic bumps. The aim was to compare the therapeutic effect of Euphorbia macrolada latex with cryotherapy in the treatment of plantar warts. In this study, 30 patients were examined and devided in two equal groups randomly. One group of patients was treated with latex of Euphorbia macrolada and the other group was treated with cryotherapy. Each patient was visited 4 times (0, 2, 4, and 12 weeks after the first treatment). Images of the lesions were captured and stored at a fixed, uniform distance by a single camera. In the group treated with the latex of euphorbia macrolada, the average wart size with 55.7% decreasing rate reached from 69.9 mm before treatment to 31 mm at the third visit (p=0.001) and two months after the last visit, it was decreased by 80% and reached to 13.9 mm (p=0.001) which in the second visit (two weeks later), all clinical findings were present in the cryotherapy group, but there was no pain or blistering in the euphorbia macrolada latex group and the incidence of tenderness, pain, and blistering in the cryotherapy group was significantly higher than other group. Considering the fewer complications and fewer recurrences of treating patients with the latex of Euphorbia macrolada, it seems that this treatment can be a suitable alternative for routine treatment with cryotherapy in the treatment of plantar warts

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Bis-Imine-Based Metal Complexes
abstract: The new bis-imine ligand was synthesized by the condensation reaction of 1- ((3-(4-fluorophenyl)-1-isopropyl-1H-indol-2-yl)methylene) hydrazine with ortho-vanillin. The synthesized ligand was subsequently employed to produce diverse transition metal complexes through the combination with suitable metal salt solutions on subsequent heating. Using UV-Vis, FTIR, 1H-NMR spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry, the functional groups, coordination interaction, and probable morphologies of the synthesized compounds were examined. On spectral data basis, it was confirmed that the ligand and its metal complexes were made. The ligand and its metal complexes were evaluated to determine their potential biological consequences. The biological activity results showed that specific metal complexes were more effective than the free ligand. Certain combinations exhibited promising effectiveness against antibacterial, anti-tuberculosis, and antimalarial activities. The results indicate that coordination of the bis-imine ligand with metal ions improves its suitability for biological activity. The indole-based bis-imine metal complexes could be ideal candidates for developing new biologically active molecules for medical applications

title: Evaluation of Adaptation Methods and Cognitive Dysfunction in Multiple Sclerosis Patients
abstract: Cognitive impairments in patients are less frequently diagnosed, which itself leads to patients using inappropriate adaptation methods. The aim of this study was to evaluate adaptation methods and cognitive dysfunction in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients. In this descriptive cross-sectional study, 100 patients with MS referred to the Neurology Clinic of Alavi in Ardabil, Iran, were evaluated. The patients completed Lazarus' Coping Strategies Questionnaire, the Adult Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and the Digit Symbol Coding Test, which were used to assess adaptation and coping methods, cognitive disorders, and processing speed, respectively. The mean age of the MS patients was 44.49±10.16 years. 76% of the participants were female, 42% were illiterate, 78% were married, and 69% were employed. The mean disease duration was 13.53±9.9 years. Among the various adaptation methods, "Accepting Responsibility" (17%) and "Seeking Social Support" (15%) were the most frequently reported, while "Positive Reappraisal" (8%) was the least used method by the patients. Routine assessment of cognitive abilities in patients with MS can help prevent their cognitive deterioration and design effective pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions

title: Polysaccharide-Derived Nanostructures: Engineering Strategies and Frontiers in Precision Nanomedicine
abstract: Nanotechnology has fundamentally revolutionized the biomedical landscape by providing high-precision solutions for diagnostics, therapeutics, and regenerative medicine. Among the myriads of available nanomaterials, carbohydrate-derived nanoparticles have emerged as premier candidates due to their superior biocompatibility, inherent biodegradability, low immunogenicity, and extensive structural versatility. This review provides a rigorous analysis of polysaccharide-based nanoparticles, delineating their primary synthetic methodologies, including ionic gelation, emulsification- solvent evaporation, and amphiphilic self-assembly, alongside critical physicochemical characterization techniques, such as dynamic light scattering and electron microscopy. A diverse library of polymers is examined, encompassing chitosan, hyaluronic acid (HA), alginate, and various microbial and marine-derived gums, each possessing unique functional moieties that facilitate specialized biological interactions. These nano constructs function as intelligent delivery vectors for pharmacological and genetic payloads, utilizing both passive accumulation via the enhanced permeation and retention (EPR) effect and active targeting through specific ligand-receptor affinities. Furthermore, their utility extends to advanced bioimaging as contrast agents, highly sensitive diagnostic biosensors, and bioactive scaffolds for tissue engineering and immunomodulation. Although challenges regarding industrial scalability and long-term toxicological profiles persist, the integration of stimuli-responsive mechanisms and theragnostic functionalities is projected to drive the next generation of personalized and efficacious nanomedicine

title: Variation in Physicochemical Content in Rhizospheric Soil Samples of Alstonia Belongs to the Same Locations
abstract: Alstonia scholaris (L.) R. Br. is an ornamental plant, commonly observed in gardens, also known as devil’s tree or dita tree. The plant is considered poisonous, and birds rarely nest on it. It belongs to the family Apocynaceae and is native to Asia and Australia. Morphologically, this tall plant has funnel shaped flowers and glossy leaves. It holds cultural significance and is used in various medicinal applications. Rhizospheric soil samples were analyzed for several parameters including pH and EC measurement, estimation of nutrients, and chlorophyll content. The species Alstonia scholaris is present on the campus of SRTM University, Nanded, which predominantly has black clay soil that is suitable. These trees are located throughout the campus and are found in the Nanded city. The plants on campus belong to the same genus and species but display differences in color of leaves and physicochemical parameters of the rhizospheric soil. All the plants are growing close to each other approximately 10 meters. With the physicochemical analysis of the soil, there were differences in the nutritional composition of the rhizospheric soil. Among all selected parameters, pH, EC, carbon content, phosphorus content, potassium content, and chlorophyll were recorded as 7.3 to 8.5, 0.16 to 0.35 dS/m, 2.8 to 6.3×103 mg/kg, 0.47 to 6.23 mg/kg, 34.9 to 927 mg/kg, and 9.72 to 21.97×10-3 mg/mL. Even when plants are in proximity, soil parameters differ. Plants do not receive the same nutrients. Variation in the pigmentation is a result of nutrient uptake by the plants reflected in leaf color variations

title: Harnessing the Power of Combination of Herbal Extracts against UTI Pathogens
abstract: Antibacterial efficacy through a synergistic approach of selective herbal extracts, i.e., amla (Emblica officinalis) druhalad (Berberis aristata) and brahmi (Bacopa monnieri) is evaluated to discover an alternative approach to control urinary-tract infections (UTIs) caused by common uropathogenic bacteria. These herbs are extracted using a Soxhlet extraction method in presence of methanol and water as solvents. The separate extracts of all medicinal herbs in both the solvents are evaluated for their antibacterial potential against common uropathogens, isolated from UTI patients. Based on morphological and biochemical tests, two microorganisms were identified as i.e., Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus. On the basis of 16S rRNA sequencing techniques, the one was identified as Kosakonia cowanii (OQ 073698), alongwith the yeast Candida albicans. Overall, significant zones of inhibition are recorded against all the uropathogens considered under study upon amla:daruhalad 7:3 (w/w) ratio in water extract with extracted yield 9.0 g/250 mL. One of the core findings from the present investigation includes the uropathogen Kosakonia cowanii is resistant to ampicillin while the above- selected screened combination of extracts is an effective and alternative treatment approach for ampicillin resistant uropathogens. This synergistic effect achieved with the tested extract combinations can provide a starting point for the development of alternative formulations, effective against the antibiotic resistant Kosakonia cowanii (OQ073698) isolate which would be effective against other uropathogens. Additionally, it was proven that these edible plant extracts could be used as natural alternative inhibitors to control microbial pathogenesis related to UTIs

title: Synthesis of Thiazoles Using Amberlyst Resin as a Reusable Heterogeneous Catalyst
abstract: Thiazole is an important five-membered heterocyclic ring containing nitrogen and sulfur atoms, playing a crucial role in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. The ring has a unique structural ability for target binding and metabolic stability, which has resulted in its utility in several commercially marketed drugs. In the present work, a rapid and efficient method has been developed for the synthesis of substituted thiazole derivatives from various substituted phenacyl bromides and thiourea in refluxing ethanol. A series of 2-amino thiazoles was synthesized in good to excellent yield of the corresponding products using Amberlyst resin as a heterogeneous catalyst. The developed protocol offers excellent yield involving a reusable catalyst and an easy work- up procedure, making the method more feasible, economical, and environmentally sustainable for the synthesis of thiazoles

title: Corrosion Inhibition Studies of Dioscorea Bulbifera Leaves Extract on Aluminum Metal in 0.6 M Hydrochloric Acid Solution
abstract: This study evaluates the corrosion inhibition performance of Dioscorea bulbifera leaf extract on aluminum in 0.6 M HCl using weight loss (ΔW) measurements at 303–323 K over 4 hours. The results show that increasing extract concentration (0.0–0.6 g) significantly reduces ΔW and corrosion rate (CR) at all temperatures. At 303 K, CR decreased from 0.035 to 0.029, while inhibition efficiency (%IE) increased slightly from 62% to approximately 63– 64%, indicating effective surface protection. A similar trend was observed at 313 K and 323 K, where CR decreased with concentration, accompanied by slight improvements in %IE. Surface coverage (θ) also increased marginally, confirming enhanced adsorption of inhibitor molecules on the aluminum surface. However, temperature had a pronounced effect on inhibition performance. As temperature increased from 303 to 323 K, CR increased while %IE decreased from 62 to 43% at the blank concentration, indicating reduced inhibitor efficiency. This decline is attributed to thermal desorption of adsorbed molecules at higher temperatures. The behavior suggests that the inhibition mechanism is predominantly governed by physisorption, involving weak intermolecular interactions. Thus, Dioscorea bulbifera extract exhibits moderate %IE, with optimal performance at lower temperatures

title: Spin-Encoded Reactivity in Monovalent Boron: Substituent-Imprinted Singlet-Triplet Signatures of Borylenes
abstract: A systematic quantum chemical investigation was carried out on sixteen monovalent B–X derivatives to elucidate substituent-controlled stabilization, electronic structure, and magnetic response in both singlet and triplet states. Calculated singlet–triplet energy gaps (ΔES-T) reveal that several substituents strongly favor singlet stabilization, with larger positive ΔE values directly correlating with enhanced thermodynamic stability. Analysis of σB-X bond energies demonstrates that stronger bonding interactions generally accompany increased singlet preference, establishing a clear energetic- structural relationship. Natural bond orbital (NBO) analysis shows that the boron lone pair (LP) in stabilized singlets possesses significant s-character, indicating pronounced electron localization rather than pure p-type behavior. Spin density calculations confirm efficient spin delocalization in triplet states, while singlets exhibit reduced magnetic perturbation at the boron center. Magnetic shielding calculations further reveal systematic variations in 11B- NMR chemical shifts consistent with changes in electronic density and bonding strength. Additionally, computed dipole moments and isotropic/anisotropic polarizabilities demonstrate that substituents modulate not only stability, but also electronic deformability and charge distribution. Overall, this study establishes quantitative correlations between ΔES-T, σB-X bond strength, hybridization patterns, NMR response, dipole moments, and polarizability, providing a unified electronic framework for understanding substituent-driven stabilization in B-centered systems

title: Global Neurocognitive Vulnerability in the Anthropocene: A Narrative Review of Physiological-Psychological Impacts of Extreme Heat and Evidence-Based Policy Interventions
abstract: The Anthropocene is characterized by an unprecedented rise in extreme heat events, posing a systemic threat to global neurocognitive health. While physiological impacts are well documented, neurocognitive vulnerabilities, ranging from acute cognitive inefficiency to heatstroke-related neuroinflammation and psychiatric morbidity, remain inadequately integrated into public health policy. The purpose of this narrative review is to synthesize multidisciplinary evidence on the physiological and psychological pathways through which extreme heat may affect cognition and mental health, and to consider the implications for heat-health policy and nature-based interventions. The review draws on targeted searches of PubMed and Google Scholar and integrates evidence across evolutionary perspectives, molecular biology, pediatrics, psychiatry, occupational health, and urban planning. Evidence indicates that acute heat exposure can impair aspects of attention, executive function, and cognitive control, although the magnitude and direction of effects vary by task, exposure intensity, acclimatization, and individual strain. Severe heat illness can involve blood-brain barrier disruption and neuroinflammatory responses, while nocturnal heat can disturb thermoregulation and sleep. Emerging human evidence also links prenatal heat exposure with neurodevelopmental outcomes, but this literature remains limited and should be interpreted cautiously. Current heat- health planning gives greater attention to physical morbidity than to mental health and neurocognitive risks. Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) may contribute to heat mitigation, although direct neurocognitive benefits require further evaluation. Eurasian Journal of Science and Technology 2026, Volume 6, Issue 4 332

title: Numerical Investigation of the Mechanical Behavior of Polyethylene Beams Containing Recycled Polyethylene
abstract: There are many types of materials, one of which is plastic materials, and among the common plastic materials is polyethylene. These materials play an important role in everyday use because they have good properties such as strength, flexibility, lightness, low cost, and better thermal properties and electrical insulation, which can be used in many industries. To enhance the performance of polymers, they are often combined with other materials to form polymer composites consisting of two or more phases, at least one of which is polymeric. By blending a polymer with another polymer or reinforcing material, unique combinations of mechanical and physical properties can be achieved. In recent years, the increasing consumption of plastics has intensified concerns regarding resource management, environmental sustainability, and plastic waste generation, leading to greater interest in recycling and reintroducing these materials into the production cycle. Characteristics such as environmental compatibility, low density, durability, favorable life-cycle performance, and cost-effectiveness have contributed to the widespread use of plastics and polymer composites in various engineering applications. In this study, virgin polyethylene was used as the matrix material and reinforced with recycled polyethylene at different weight ratios, including a specimen composed entirely of recycled polyethylene. The objective of this research was to determine the optimal recycled polyethylene content for practical applications while maintaining suitable mechanical performance. Based on the simulation and mechanical analysis results, the composite containing 30% recycled polyethylene exhibited the best balance between mechanical strength, dimensional stability, and reduced consumption of virgin material

title: Recent Advances in Synthesis, Characterization, and Applications of Schiff Base Ligands: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Schiff base ligands have attracted considerable attention in modern chemistry due to their facile synthesis, structural diversity, and wide range of applications in coordination chemistry, medicinal chemistry, catalysis, and materials science. These compounds are commonly prepared through condensation reactions between primary amines and carbonyl compounds, producing the characteristic azomethine (–C=N–) functional group responsible for their versatile chemical behavior. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in synthesis and characterization of new Schiff base ligands. Different synthetic approaches, including conventional reflux methods, green synthesis strategies, microwave-assisted techniques, and solvent-free procedures, are discussed with emphasis on their advantages and limitations. Furthermore, important characterization techniques such as FTIR, NMR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, X- ray diffraction, and thermal analysis are summarized to highlight their role in structural confirmation and property evaluation. The biological, catalytic, environmental, and material applications of Schiff base ligands and their metal complexes are also reviewed. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives regarding sustainable synthesis, advanced functional materials, and biomedical applications are discussed. This review highlights the continuing importance of Schiff base chemistry and its potential contribution to the development of multifunctional compounds for future technological and scientific applications. The review also briefly highlights the emerging electrochemical and bioanalytical applications of Schiff base ligands, which represent a growing area of interest
